context: Everything needed comes from the simulated one-way offers for ORD (Chicago O'Hare) to LHR (London Heathrow) on 2026-11-19, as returned by the flight search for that route and local date. The booking date is 2026-11-12 (UTC); the travel date is the local date at the origin. Fares are in US cents; schedules, fares and open seats are simulated and deterministic, and the search lists every offer for that route and day (airline, flight numbers, local departure/arrival, stops, total minutes, time_of_day, open_seats, fare_cents, segments). Use exactly those offers; there is no other data source. A booking picks one offer and one seat type from that offer's open_seats (WINDOW, AISLE or MIDDLE). Score = seat_weight if the seat equals seat_preference (MIDDLE never does) + time_weight if offer.time_of_day equals time_preference + stops_weight if stops_preference is NONSTOP and offer.stops == 0, or stops_preference is CONNECTING and offer.stops >= 1. time_of_day is DAY when the first flight departs 06:00-20:55 local time at the origin, RED_EYE when 21:00-23:55 (the search labels it). Pick the booking with the highest possible score over every offer and open seat; among the offers that can reach that highest score, pick one with the lowest fare_cents (any of them on an exact fare tie), and book any open seat on it that reaches the highest score. Nothing else counts: not total_minutes, not the airline, not the arrival time, and fare only as the tie-break. The three weights in the input add up to 100.
